verdict_last_change.evidence: The change shipped 2026-07-23 - the SAME day this window ends - so the 14 days ending 2026-07-23 contain essentially NO post-change traffic; the 42.2% (65/154) vs 39.8% (64/161) figures are the current gate state, NOT a before/after of this change, and they are flat and well inside the noise floor either way (p=0.66; ~16pt minimum detectable). The change shipped labelled unmeasurable-by-design with its own re-measure date of 2026-08-05, once the durable page_viewed->email_field_engaged->email_entered split has ~2 weeks of post-07-22 data. Verdict stays not_yet_measurable and the entry carries forward; it may NOT be claimed as a win without a SIGNIFICANT result.

leaks_ranked.step: Claim page: landed -> gave email (the QR-scan email gate)
leaks_ranked.why_real: Largest single drop by headcount in the whole funnel and stable across both windows (39.8% -> 42.2%, p=0.66 flat, not a one-window blip). Corroborated by an independent instrument: session-replay metadata shows 61% (19/31) of in-window claim sessions never type a single key. Two sources agree the gate loses ~58-61% of scanners.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Top of funnel, so it multiplies everything downstream, and it feeds the DOMINANT review engine: over 30d the in-app thank-you screen produced 16 of 21 (76%) of all review clicks, and that screen is reachable ONLY via email -> app -> video. Roughly 11 in-app review clicks came from 65 email captures this window (~0.17 reviews per captured email). A +5pt capture lift (~+7-8 emails/fortnight) plausibly yields ~+1.3 extra reviews/fortnight, compounding - modest in isolation but the highest-leverage step because it is upstream of ~all reviews.

leaks_ranked.step: In-app: arrived -> started a video (warm users, already gave email)
leaks_ranked.why_real: ~53 of 85 warm, already-committed users are lost before a video starts; persistent across windows (p=0.75 flat, i.e. a stable leak not a blip). Directly feeds the in-app thank-you review screen - the dominant review engine.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: High per-head value (these users already cleared the gate and were promised a free video), but it was genuinely attacked TWICE recently - 2026-06-16 hero bundle (worked) and 2026-07-06 message-friction (pending) - so it is recently-touched and its latest reading is not in yet. Piling another change here now would muddy that read.

leaks_ranked.prior_rate: 2 clicks (preview receiver) in the prior 14d window
leaks_ranked.why_real: Real preview/share traffic (preview_opened 29 this window, share_page_opened 20) yet almost no review clicks - a genuine structural under-performance, not noise.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Directly feeds reviews but tiny in absolute terms (3/21 over 30d, mostly one surface) and already reworked once in June with no effect. Closing it fully might add ~1-2 reviews/month - smaller than the two above.

biggest_leak: The claim-page email gate (landed -> gave email): it is the largest headcount drop, sits at the very top so it multiplies downstream, and is the single gate to the dominant in-app review engine (76% of 30d reviews) - the highest value-to-reviews of any step, and the least-worked given only two single-mechanism attempts ever.

choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: Every review-producing path starts with an email: the in-app thank-you screen (16/21 = 76% of 30d review clicks) requires email -> app -> video -> thankyou, and the Klaviyo reminder emails (email_redirect: 2/21) require the address. At ~0.17 in-app reviews per captured email, a small durable capture lift compounds directly into reviews. Downstream review engines can only ever act on the ~42% who clear this gate, so lifting the gate raises the ceiling for all of them at once.
choice_reasoning.already_tried_here: Coverage map: 2 real conversion attempts. PR #8 rebuilt the layout/hierarchy -> flat (44.5% -> 39.0%). 2026-07-23 reworded two lines of opening voice -> shipped, unmeasurable, pending. Plus INFRA-only instrumentation (07-20, 07-22) and two OWNER-REJECTED ideas (discount-first; printed-% gap). Per the rules a single failed/shipped mechanism fences only that mechanism - the distrust, hidden-emotional-hook, single-value, no-reason-now and felt-cost causes have never been attacked here.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all changes: the one thing that MOVED this funnel was a concrete mechanism change with a real reason (2026-06-16 email-first delivery + value-prop hero: +14pts in-app, held 3 weeks). The things that did NOTHING were a generic presentation reshuffle (PR #8) and word-only tweaks. That argues for a specific, mechanism-driven change with a tangible lever - here, surfacing a real IMAGE that already exists but is hidden - over another copy pass or another vague reshuffle.
choice_reasoning.why_not_the_others: In-app arrived->video is high-value but was attacked twice in the last ~5 weeks and its 07-06 read is still pending - touching it now would confound that measurement. Preview/share review asks feed reviews directly but are tiny in absolute volume (3/21 over 30d) and already reworked once with no effect. The Klaviyo reminder emails are out of this repo's scope. The email gate is bigger, upstream of both other review engines, and the least-worked by distinct mechanism.

diagnosis.question: Why do ~58% of QR scanners who land on claim.html never submit an email - are they never engaging (first-paint / never reached the field) or engaging-then-declining (form friction or a declined trade)?
hypotheses_considered: Broken emotional thread: the box earns the scan through affection for a handmade gift, but the page hides the gift (product-showcase is display:none) and greets that affection with a coupon + email field, so the first-paint impression is a marketing form and people pattern-match 'coupon form -> close tab'.
Discount-ceiling: a share never intended to claim a NEXT-order discount (one-off gift buyers / recipients) - a real ceiling no page change moves.
Distrust: an unfamiliar QR domain asking for an email before giving anything reads as a spam trap.
Form friction: people engage the field and fail (typo/validation/keyboard).
Never reached the field: bounced/confused/slow load before seeing the ask.
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Watched the metadata of all 31 in-window claim-page session recordings via the PostHog recordings API (keypress/click/duration per session). 61% (19/31) never typed a key; only 12/31 typed at all; of the 19 never-typers, 6 clicked nothing and 13 clicked something without typing; never-typer durations spread 4x <=5s, 6x 6-20s, 5x 21-60s, 4x >60s. Cross-checked capture rate in PostHog (person-linked) across both frozen windows (42.2% vs 39.8%). Verified in code that the character image IS fetched on load but its container is display:none (claim.html:1044; api/product-lookup builds images/<character>-buyer.jpg; assets present).
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: The loss is overwhelmingly BEFORE field engagement: only ~39% (12/31) ever type, and nearly all real losers never touch the field. Form friction is largely ruled out (too few typers to explain a 58% loss). So the leverage is at first paint / the reason-to-engage, not at the input mechanics - exactly where surfacing the emotional hero image acts.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: The instrument cannot separate 'never engaged because the page failed to connect emotionally' from 'never engaged because they don't want a next-order discount (ceiling)'. The 13 clicked-but-never-typed and the 4 who lingered >60s are exactly this ambiguous middle. The durable page_viewed->email_field_engaged->email_entered split that would quantify never-engaged vs engaged-declined does not read cleanly until ~2026-08-05 (both windows must sit on/after the 07-22 instrument fix). So the MAGNITUDE of the winnable share is a genuine bet; the LOCATION of the loss (first paint) is evidenced.

plan.title: Bring the crochet friend on-screen: surface the already-fetched product character as a warm first-paint hero on the claim page
plan.targets: Claim page: landed -> gave email (first-paint engagement of the ~58-61% who currently never engage the email field)
plan.mechanism: The one asset that earned the scan - the handmade crochet character the visitor is holding - is already fetched by init() from /api/product-lookup and assigned to #productImage on every load, but its parent .product-showcase is hard-coded display:none (claim.html:1044), so the page opens with a coupon and an email field while the gift stays invisible. Un-hide and position that character image (with its product name) as a compact, premium emotional hero directly under the warm kicker 'Hope it made you smile', ABOVE the reward list and form. This re-connects the box->page emotional thread with a real IMAGE (a stronger lever than words) at the exact moment the loss happens - first paint - earning a second beat of attention from scanners who would otherwise pattern-match 'marketing form -> close' before they weigh the trade.
plan.assumed_cause: Broken emotional thread / the delight is invisible: the page hides the handmade gift and leads with a coupon, so the first-paint impression fails to connect with the affection that earned the scan, and a share of scanners disengage before reaching (or committing to) the email field.

cause_verification.for: Session-recording metadata for all 31 in-window claim sessions: 61% (19/31) never typed a key and only 12/31 typed at all, so the loss lives BEFORE field engagement - precisely the first-paint moment this image acts on. 10 of the 19 never-typers left within 20s (4x <=5s, 6x 6-20s), consistent with a first-impression bounce. Verified in code that the emotional asset exists and is fetched but rendered invisible (display:none at claim.html:1044), so there is a concrete, fixable page defect between the box's promise and the page's first paint.
cause_verification.against: I actively looked for two things that would kill this cause. (1) Form-friction: if most non-submitters had TYPED and failed, an image above the fold would not help - but only 12/31 typed at all, so engaged-then-failed cannot explain a ~58% loss; the cause survives. (2) Discount-ceiling / not-interested: I checked whether the never-typers look like people who simply do not want a next-order discount - 13/19 clicked something and 4 lingered >60s yet still declined, which the instrument CANNOT distinguish from 'not emotionally pulled'. That is the honest contradicting signal: an unknown slice of the loss may be a ceiling no image moves, so I did not find evidence that fully clears the cause for that middle group.
cause_verification.why_for_wins: The location of the loss (first paint, pre-engagement) is evidenced by two independent sources and matches exactly where this change acts; the strongest lever available for a first-impression is a real image, not more words. Where the evidence cannot settle magnitude (the discount-ceiling middle), the change is a cheap, reversible bet that ALSO fixes a verified defect - a page about a handmade gift that hides the gift - so it is worth making regardless of how large the winnable share turns out to be. Critically, it is NOT a fix aimed at a cause the data disproves (the last cycle's failure mode); it is aimed at the cause the data supports, with its one unprovable assumption stated plainly.

plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: The gate is an exchange: the visitor hands over an email to get the 30% code and the free video. Converters accept that price because the reward feels real and worth it in the moment. Non-converters, at first paint, are shown a coupon and a form with no emotional anchor to the gift they already love - so the perceived worth of the trade is set by a marketing-form impression rather than by the handmade character that motivated the scan. Raising the felt worth of the page at first paint (showing their friend) is meant to move more people to accept the SAME exchange - it does NOT touch the price (email still required) or what is delivered.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A non-trivial share of the ~58% who never engage are leaving because the first-paint impression fails to connect emotionally, not purely because they never wanted a next-order discount.

The scanning SKUs resolve to a video character so characterImage is non-null and a real portrait renders (top SKUs PTT-GREEN1/FRIENDFUN/CPCK1 map to characters; products with no character keep today's behaviour - the empty container renders nothing).
A single premium 120px portrait under the kicker reads as warmth/legitimacy, not as clutter that pushes the reward and CTA meaningfully down.
plan.second_order_effects: The same character already autoplays as a video preview at the BOTTOM of the page; adding a still portrait at the top creates mild repetition, but the two do different jobs (identity/emotional anchor at first paint vs 'here's what you'll create' tease below the fold that non-engagers never scroll to) and the top placement is where the loss occurs. The image is ALREADY downloaded on load (imgEl.src is set regardless of display), so un-hiding adds zero network bytes - only a decode/paint - so LCP/latency risk is negligible. It pushes the reward list and form down by one compact element; on mobile the kicker+portrait+reward-intro should still sit at/near the top of the first viewport. No gate, reward, delivery path, or promise is touched, so there is no downstream review cost.
plan.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the 61% who never type may simply not want a next-order discount (a ceiling no portrait moves), and the character is not truly 'invisible' - the same character autoplays as a video lower down - so this just adds a heavy portrait that shoves the actual reward and CTA further from the top, delaying the ask for the people who WOULD have converted. My answer: (1) the image is already fetched, so there is no added latency, and a 120px portrait is compact - the reward list and form remain immediately below, not materially displaced; (2) the bottom video sits below the fold precisely where non-engagers never scroll, so it does no first-paint work - the whole point is to put the friend where first paint actually is; (3) the ceiling risk is real and acknowledged, which is exactly why this is labelled measurable:false and shipped as a cheap, reversible bet rather than a claimed win - and even under the sceptic's worst case it corrects a genuine defect (a handmade-gift page that hides the gift). If the 2026-08-05 split shows the loss is mostly a discount-ceiling, the next swing pivots to the discount-indifferent segment (e.g. the video co-hero angle).
plan.expected_effect: A few points of extra email capture at best (well inside the noise floor at ~150 landers/fortnight), by earning first-paint engagement from a slice of the ~58% who currently never touch the field. Directionally lifts every downstream review path since all of them start at this gate.

tradeoff.gained: A warm, on-brand first-paint impression that reconnects the box's promise to the page and gives first-paint non-engagers a reason to look twice before deciding - aimed at the largest, highest-value, least-worked leak.
tradeoff.risked: Negligible measurable downside: no gate, reward, delivery, or promise changes, so the review paths it feeds (in_app thankyou 16/21 and email_redirect 2/21 over 30d) are untouched - this cannot reduce email capture the way the owner-rejected discount-first idea would. The only real risks are null effect (the loss is a discount-ceiling the image can't move) or minor visual clutter; both are fully reversible by re-adding display:none.

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: PR #8 (spent ground) was a generic full-page layout/hierarchy REBUILD that never surfaced this hidden image - a different mechanism (structure vs imagery). The 2026-07-23 change reworded two LINES of copy - words, not imagery. Neither owner rejection applies: this never hands the discount code over before the email (discount-first, rejected 2026-07-20) and never references or compares to the printed percentage (printed-% gap, rejected 2026-07-19). It is a specific, mechanism-driven imagery change, not PR #8's vague reshuffle.
plan.how_to_verify: Build: remove display:none from .product-showcase (keep the img/name .hidden toggles so no-character SKUs render nothing). Boot locally (PORT=3939 node --experimental-websocket server.js), fetch claim.html?sku=PTT-GREEN1 and ?sku=PTT-CPCK1 -> confirm the character portrait + product name render as a hero under the kicker, above the reward list; fetch a no-character SKU -> confirm graceful fallback (no empty/broken image, layout intact); confirm the 30% reward, 'Send Me My Code' button, email field, gate, and video preview are all unchanged. Render mobile before/after PNGs. Delete any page_viewed test rows created by the screenshot loads. Re-measure the durable gate split on 2026-08-05 via linked-funnel page_viewed->email_field_engaged and email_field_engaged->email_entered (both windows on/after 07-22), then significance-test - though at this traffic it will likely stay inside the noise floor.
alternatives_rejected: Calm the scam-signal first paint (soften confetti/blur/prize popup): higher potential swing but touches a celebratory reveal the owner may value, higher risk and lower certainty, and bets on a distrust cause the data cannot confirm.
Real-maker legitimacy / trust block: a bet on distrust the data can't yet confirm; lower confidence than fixing a verified page defect.

Video-as-co-hero above the fold: a bet on the discount-indifferent segment's size (unsettled until ~08-05); a good NEXT swing if the split shows a large ceiling, but weaker evidence now than the hidden-image defect.

CTA button relabel/restyle, urgency 'reserved for you' cue, field-level reassurance: lower-confidence bets on causes (weak-value, no-reason-now, felt-cost) that the never-typer evidence makes secondary to first-paint non-engagement.
Discount-first and printed-% reveal: owner-rejected, off-limits.
